name: Clusters of short-lived storms (multicells)
line: Weaker wind shear: new storms keep forming along the spreading cold air as the old ones rain out.
note: CM1's own analytic sounding with its multicell wind profile. The area is not made smaller than 120 km, because CM1's parcel grid covers 120 km; the fit makes the grid coarser or the storm shorter instead.

changes.why: a picture every 5 minutes, so the live view moves
CM1's multicell wind profile (Weisman and Klemp 1982)
netCDF, which ncview, xarray and most tools read (CM1's file asks for GrADS)
one file per saved time, so each picture has its own file
follow air parcels, so Results can show air rising into the storm
CM1's own parcel grid: 60 x 60 across, every 2 km, and 10 levels, every 1 km
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)

gm1_settings_why: The warm bubble that starts the storm sits 7.6 km east and 7.8 km south of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the bubble in its code, not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.
